text: The CNG and the CPN shall support adequate Quality of Service mechanisms (e.g. prioritize the traffic in the event that there is not sufficient bandwidth in the customer network in order to ensure the correct network performances to each traffic flow). To achieve this objective a number of functionalities shall be supported by CNG and/or CNDs as defined in the following bullets. Most of the following set of requirements is defined adopting as a reference the Home Gateway Initiative (HGI) Release 1 Specification mentioned in clause 2 [6].
label: Performance

text: The NGN network QoS functions shall be possible to use to enhance the end-user experience.
label: Performance

text: The CNG may interact with the Resource and Admission Control Subsystem (RACS) as defined in ES 282 001 [9] to support remote real-time QoS control
label: Performance

text: The CNG may interact with network elements inside the CPN to support QoS control inside the CPN.
label: Performance

text: The CNG shall classify packets entering the CPN through its WAN interface (downstream direction) according to a number of predefined priorities. Classification can be done on the basis of different layer 2 and/or layer 3 parameters.
label: Performance

text: The number of possible values defining the packet priority and by consequence the number of queues managed in the downstream direction shall be coherent with the number of concurrent services (data communication entertainment) to be treated and supported.
label: Performance

text: When forwarding packets from the WAN interface to the customer network the CNG shall perform one of the following three actions depending on the classification results: manage a number of queues corresponding to the different priorities detected in the classification phase for each packet processed send the packets to some internal buffers or simply drop the packet.
label: Performance

text: The CNG shall classify packets coming from the CPN through its LAN interfaces (upstream direction) according to a number of predefined priorities. Classification can be done on the basis of different layer 2 and/or layer 3 parameters.
label: Performance

text: The number of possible values defining the packet priority and by consequence the number of queues managed in the upstream direction shall be coherent with the number of concurrent services (data communication entertainment) to be treated and supported.
label: Performance

text: When forwarding packets from the customer network to the WAN interface the CNG shall manage a number of queues corresponding to the different priorities detected in the classification phase for each packet processed.
label: Performance

text: The CNG shall be able to classify intra-LAN traffic that is simply bridged by the CNG itself within the CPN.
label: Performance

text: Traffic marking: depending on what are the parameters used to perform classification CNDs or CNG itself on behalf of the CNDs shall be able to modify the packets' priority.
label: Performance

text: In case of huge amount of traffic in upstream or downstream directions a congestion management mechanism shall be implemented in the CNG to minimize the impact from the user experience point of view.
label: Performance

text: In case of managed services QoS rules applied by CNG shall be configurable by a remote management system.
label: Performance

text: It shall be possible to configure the CNG (e.g. firmware downloading) according to the subscribed services. This operation may be performed when the CNG is connected to the network for the first time for each new service subscription/modification or for any technical management (e.g. security patches etc.).
label: Security

label: Security

text: Protection mechanisms shall be implemented to avoid that a management client could access and modify parameters that is not allow to configure.
label: Security
